_comment: Research, Security and Practice section sources for Securesein. Same conventions as feeds-releases.json: tier=primary may trigger a post, corroborating may only support one, community is context only. verified=true means the URL was fetched and returned parseable entries on 2026-09-14; everything else must be checked with verify_feeds.py before use. The 'section' field is the default section for items from this source — the classifier may override it, but a source whose items are constantly reclassified is mistiered and should be fixed here.

feeds.note: The missing arXiv category — cs.CL and cs.LG are already in feeds.json but LLM attack papers land in cs.CR. High volume; the quality gate does the filtering.
Very high volume. Consider enabling only after the quality gate has been calibrated on cs.CL/cs.LG.
Anthropic's interpretability publication. Closest match in the entire feed set to the strongest stated interest in the profile — treat a new item here as near-automatic Research material.
Mechanism-first explanations at exactly the depth the profile rewards. Also useful as a style reference for the Fundamentals section.
Infrequent, consistently high quality. Low volume means it rarely competes for budget.
Weekly roundup. Useful for discovering papers, but a roundup is not a primary source — never publish a post whose only source is another roundup.

feeds.scopeNote: verify_feeds 2026-09-14: FAIL (connection timeout, retried once by hand with the same result). Host-side, not a URL error — bair.berkeley.edu did not answer at all. Left IN SCOPE and untouched: the adapter is failure-isolated, so an unreachable host costs one empty list per run, and guessing at a new URL for a blog that is probably just down would be worse than waiting.

feeds.note: Analysis arm of the same organisation whose data drives the Benchmarks section. Good source for trend claims that can be checked against the benchmarks collection.
Practical applied research, often about making things run on modest hardware — matches the inference-efficiency interest.
The single most consistently productive source on practical prompt injection and agent hijacking. If only one security feed survives verification, make it this one.
3 entries on test. Low frequency; a release here is a genuine editorial event and a good anchor for an explainer.
10 entries on test. New probes indicate which attack classes are becoming mainstream. Tool releases themselves are rarely post-worthy; the probe taxonomy is.
10 entries on test. Defensive tooling side of the same picture.
10 entries on test.
10 entries on test. New tactics/techniques in the ATLAS matrix are the closest thing to an authoritative taxonomy update for AI attacks — directly usable in client-facing material.
10 entries on test. Evaluation framework used for pre-deployment safety testing; changes here affect how safety evals are run and reported.
10 entries on test. MCP server security — the supply-chain surface that matters most as agents reach enterprise environments.
10 entries on test. Context only — this is an ecosystem signal, not a security finding.
Rigorous, occasional AI/ML security work. High signal when it appears.
Vendor research. Real findings, but read as marketing-adjacent — the quality gate's source_quality component should reflect that.
Filter to AI items. Relevant where it changes what a practitioner must do (AI RMF, control mappings), not for announcements.
EU angle. Relevant to BIO2/NLMAPGOV-adjacent work; low volume.
